title: Voyager Web Design v2 — screenshots-grounded
notes:
v2 of the Voyager web-design rubric. Built from PNG screenshots in /home/tk/voyager/shots/ + the extracted-tokens JSON at the same path. v0.1 (advisory-call-grounded) at /home/tk/rubric/rubrics/voyager_web_design.json is unmodified and remains valid; this v2 sits alongside as a broader-evidence counterpart.

Refutation from slice A (gov/cultural evidence): v0.1 C5's '≤20 words above the fold' was implicit about a value-statement job. visitbarbados's actual hero is a Customs/Immigration compliance banner ('Arriving in Barbados soon? Please make sure to fill out your Online Customs and Immigration form before your arrival'). Government-affiliated tourism sites may legitimately use the hero for compliance, not aspiration. v2's C5 below admits both as legitimate one-job-per-screen.

build_provenance.method: COLLECT → ANALYZE → CONTRAST → DRAFT per the rubric-authoring skill
vision_evidence_sites: + subagent B report of 12 music-artist sites (file: _slice_B_report.json)
+ subagent A report of 10 gov/cultural sites (return-message received 2026-09-03 00:08:42; file not written to disk — content recovered from inline return)
+ subagent C report of 6 festival/industry + negative-register sites (received 2026-09-03 00:27:18, 26m53s after dispatch — longest silent stretch)
build_provenance.tokens_json_evidence_sites: 29 entries total — all sites in the shots directory have either vision or token evidence (overlap)
build_provenance.spec_reduction_reason: vision was heavy (each call dumps full pixels into context); after 12 sites the converging themes were clear — continuing all 28 would burn context without changing the rubric. tokens.json stat-scan provided the remaining signal at low cost.
build_provenance.methodology_notes_for_reviewer: v0.1's criteria (7 criteria: C1-C7) were tested against the wider vision evidence; some were confirmed unchanged, some were narrowed, one was DROPPED (C2 'one warm accent for CTA' — fails on rihanna/beyonce/bobmarley which use B&W-only restraint), and three NEW criteria emerged that the v0.1 evidence set could not have caught because the v0.1 set was 4 sites all in the same register.

register_taxonomy_discovered.civic_ocean_register (COR): Public-sector / tourism-board / civic body. Navy/teal + warm accent + photographic hero. visitbarbados, caribbeanbeat, socanews.
register_taxonomy_discovered.editorial_discipline_register (EDC): Iconic artist / beauty brand. B&W restraint, no CTA, custom-display sans or no display at all, large negative space. bobmarley, rihanna, beyonce, fenty.
register_taxonomy_discovered.cultural_distinct_register (CDR): Contemporary music / diaspora community / carnival. Cultural script lettering, festival-poster aesthetics, handcraft palette, photographic hero with painted/illustration overlay. largeup, koffee, machel, wiadca.
register_taxonomy_discovered.platform_extraction_register (PEX) — out: Generic CMS / SPA / dynamic-pricing platform. Empty art tiles, anti-patterns, surveillance-theatre, no cultural specificity. spotify, ticketmaster, travelocity.

criteria.name: Caribbean-cultural anchoring (the unifying class criterion)
criteria.what_it_checks: The site declares a real cultural commitment somewhere on the surface — community, place, performance, diaspora, history, language — and that declaration is from the inside, not stock imagery imported from outside.
criteria.observable: At least one of: visible Caribbean place-name or person (not as decoration), local language register in copy, community-association or artist-or-organizer byline (not corporate legal-fine-print), diaspora-coded iconography (carnival regalia, soca/dancehall/calypso framing), brand name that roots in place (not generic travel/CMS). NOT measurable by cultural stock photos alone.

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: Cultural anchor is plainly front-facing: real named community/artist/place, local register in copy, bylines or affiliations that read as from-the-inside.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: Cultural anchoring present and mostly lived-in, but one section defaults to corporate or stock language.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Only second-order signals: a logo, a stock beach photo, a stock-phrase copyright. No real declaration.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: Cultural specificity is absent or only geographic in the URL. Generic SaaS or platform-shell register. (This is the spotify/ticketmaster register.)

criteria.generation_rule:
Pick ONE anchor element — community name, artist/creator credit, place + practice — and surface it in the hero or footer where a sign-up signal usually lives. Don't say 'we celebrate Caribbean culture' — show who and where and when. Where appropriate, allow vernacular/dialect in nav labels (seanpaul.com's 'Yaad', 'Chunes', 'Pree Dis', 'Dutty Rock' as a register-allowed authentic signal), and where the work has credibility carry it visibly (festival laurels / press strip / 'as seen in' module — a Caribbean-artist social-proof convention).

For civic/cultural/regional sites, anchor in a Caribbean flag or land signal (specific maroon / ultramarine / gold / sky-blue / magenta-feather), include a named civic body / byline / issue stamp where the work is journalism or governance, and acknowledge diaspora awareness when the register is cross-Atlantic carnival (caribana/Toronto + nottinghill/London pattern — different palettes but same host-city-diaspora remit).
pitfalls: Stock beach/palm-tree cliche used as the primary Caribbean signal
Generic 'travel' or 'tickets' website with no community or creator visibility
Caribbean-coded content but corporate-themed chrome (every visual register contradicts the message)
Cultural-specificity present but coded as 'tropical' rather than real place/practice
Replacing photography with vector pillar-icons / flag-only chrome (caricom four-pillar icon set — reads like a UN agency, not a Caribbean community)
Compliance banner in hero treated as off-brand — it isn't, when the site genuinely has a compliance gatekeeping role

Substituting a brand-name H1 ('CARICOM' / 'PMO' / 'Soca News' literal wordmark) for a value statement — except for the few cases where the brand-name H1 IS the value statement (e.g. visitbarbados wordmark-as-place-mark)

criteria.negative_passes_if_offclass: spotify/ticketmaster/travelocity — generic platform, no Caribbean anchor → fails on this criterion

criteria.name: Disciplined palette within a register family
criteria.what_it_checks: The site commits to ONE palette family — civic-ocean (navy/teal/cream + warm accent), editorial (B&W + custom display), or cultural-distinct (cultural iconography + warm/painted colors) — and uses it within that register instead of drifting across all three.
criteria.observable: Dominant ground color (top-1 by coverage) plus dominant text/display color (top-1 by frequency) plus 1-2 accent fills — totals to 3-4 named colors, each serving a defined role (ground / type / action / highlight). No 'kitchen-sink' mixing of all three register palettes on one surface.

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: Three to four named colors, each playing a defined role; surfaces commit to ONE register family.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: Right register, but one section drifts to a competing register (e.g. a B&W brand suddenly runs a magenta promo band).

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Mostly disciplined but no clear ground/text/action hierarchy — colors share visual weight.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: Three-register mixing across sections (navy civic + B&W editorial + painted-cultural on the same surface), corporate blue SaaS default, or sunset-gradient laziness.

criteria.generation_rule: Pick a register first (civic / editorial / cultural-distinct). Within that register, choose a ground color (top-1 by coverage), a near-black or near-white text, and at most two accent fills. Hierarchy by tonal value, not by hue variety.
pitfalls: Three registers mixed because the brand couldn't decide
Sunset-gradient of every Caribbean-flag color (national-flag tokenism masquerading as design)
Bright-everything (no ground, no discipline, no hierarchy)
SSA-SaaS-blue + orange used as a substitute for commitment
Generic institutional blue/grey chrome where Caribbean palette is missing (pmo_barbados, nottinghill, caricom UN-agency read)

Using only national-flag tokens (red/gold/black for one site) instead of register-appropriate palette (a culture magazine / civic body / diaspora carnival each have non-flag palettes that are still legitimate)
evidence: visitbarbados: navy ground + gold + white = clean civic-ocean register
bobmarley + beyonce + rihanna + fenty: B&W or near-B&W ground with restrained single accent (or none) = editorial register
largeup + koffee: warm cultural-distinct (gold/cream/red-painted + ocean blue + wood) = legitimate third register

Caribbean flag-palette anchors (real hexes from tokens.json): maroon #660028 (windies), ultramarine #0028a7 (alisonhinds_tourism), gold #fbed00 (windies CTA), near-black #0a0a0a for body + maroon nav band
Magenta H1 #ed177a (caribana) + violet #9e5aff body = diaspora-carnival non-flag palette, register-allowed
Regalia-palette exceptions (white + red logo + charcoal nav band on caribbeanbeat / largeup) = editorial-discipline register, also register-allowed
criteria.v0_1_change: v0.1's C1 'ocean-teal anchor' and C2 'sunshine + carnival accent' BOTH survive here as parts of one wider criterion: any of the three register palettes is acceptable; the invariant is discipline within a register. This criterion is now register-invariant and harder to game by painting Caribbean-flag colors.

criteria.name: Black-ground, high-contrast type (or near-equivalent)
criteria.what_it_checks: Type sits at strong contrast against its surface — body ≥4.5:1, display ≥3:1 (WCAG AA), and the dominant text-on-ground pairing either reads near-black on warm/light or reads light on dark, never muddled-gray on muddled-gray.
criteria.observable: Body text contrast ratio ≥4.5:1; display text ≥3:1; near-black type (#000..#1a1a22) on warm cream / white / single-tone ground; or reversed to light on dark. No gray-on-gray body; no thin hairline borders as the only elevation cue.

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: Body passes AA against surface; hierarchy expressed by size/weight/value, not by added hues.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: Mostly AA-compliant, but one section uses mid-gray body or a single low-contrast muted band.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Body text gray-on-white (#a8a8a8-class) in places; contrast fixed with thin borders or filter overlays instead of tonal value.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: Muddled mid-tones throughout, or all-black-everything that drops the register anchor.

criteria.generation_rule: Body/display type near-black on warm/light, or clean reverse on a single dark section. Verify AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large). Hierarchy by tonal value, not by additional chrome.
pitfalls: Gray-on-gray body text
Black-everything that forgets the register anchor
Thin hairline borders as the only elevation cue
Brighter than #a8a8a8 body on white surface
evidence: tokens.json: 10/16 remaining sites use white #fff canvas, 5/16 use near-black #000 body text — universal default
bobmarley: B&W crowd photo + dark hero with high-contrast white display
fenty: extreme B&W discipline — the brand itself

criteria.name: Display voice committed (or purposefully absent)
criteria.what_it_checks: If a display face is used, it's a bold/condensed/hand-crafted family at weight ≥600 and clear scale. If the design intentionally uses NO display (editorial discipline), the bodies/headlines are also disciplined and sit at considered sizes — neither register bleeds into generic system-sans defaults.
criteria.observable: Display families fall into one of two committed kinds: (a) condensed bold sans (Bebas Neue / Oswald / Intro / Montserrat Bold class), (b) hand-script or festival-poster display (Bangers / custom hand / painted-type). Body uses a clean humanist sans (Open Sans / Manrope / Roboto / Raleway / Helvetica/Arial-class). NO mixed-mash of 4+ faces. NO system-serif editorial stack.

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: Display committed (condensed bold OR handcraft) at weight ≥600 with clear scale; body is a clean sans; the type system reads as one choice.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: Right families, but display weight or size is timid, or body defaults to system sans with no humanist character.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Default system sans throughout (no display voice), or body set in a slab/serif that fights the display.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: Full serif editorial (Didot/Times), font soup (4+ families with no scale), or system-default-stack-everywhere.

criteria.generation_rule: Display: condensed bold (Bebas Neue / Oswald / Intro / Montserrat Bold class) OR handcraft (Bangers / custom hand / painted). Body: Open Sans / Manrope / Roboto / Raleway / Helvetica-class. No serif above body size unless the design is deliberately editorial.
pitfalls: Serif 'premium editorial' headline on a community site
Default system sans with no display voice
Font soup (4+ families, no scale)
Bangers + Arial body — playful headline + boring body, no system
Type-scale drift (60+px accidental jump between display and body — e.g. 72px h1 over 10px body reads as uncalibrated, not typographic)
All-caps nav with no italic/underline on hover (visually clean but read-aloud-accessibility-hostile)
H1 font-size equals body font-size (socanews 14px = 14px — flat hierarchy)
H1 token text is empty string when computed — visitbarbados hero was a compliance banner that consumed the visible H1
evidence: tokens.json: Bebas Neue + Oswald + Manrope (bobmarley), Bangers + sans (festival/carnival register), Montserrat / Roboto / Open Sans / Raleway across body sites
largeup: handwritten script logo + clean body sans — committed two-voice system
koffee: handcrafted painted display + warm-gold ground — committed
fentybeauty ships a 72px display over a 10px body — accidental scale drift, not design
criteria.v0_1_change: v0.1's C4 ('Bold display type, clean sans body') retained AND widened to admit the handcraft/hand-script path that v0.1 missed. v0.1 allowed only the condensed-bold display family; v2 legitimizes Bangers/handcraft/painted too because largeup and koffee use it successfully.

criteria.name: One job per screen, visible above the fold
criteria.what_it_checks: Every screen has a single job. Above the fold, the visitor sees at most ONE primary statement (≤20 words where the design supports it, OR no statement at all in editorial-discipline register) and at most ONE primary action.
criteria.observable: Above the fold: ≤20 words of primary statement OR deliberately empty (editorial register), and at most ONE primary CTA visible. Across the page: no carousel, no interstitial gate, no forced-steps funnel.

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: ≤20 words above the fold (or none, in editorial), one primary action visible; nothing decorative blocking it.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: Right structure, but hero is slightly crowded or the statement drifts past 20 words.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Multiple competing statements, or auto-rotating carousel, or a sticker-countdown widget layering urgency onto the hero.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: Multiple hero blocks, forced-steps funnel, modal interstitial, three competing CTAs, or 'splash then gate' route.

criteria.generation_rule: One job per screen. Above the fold, name product/audience in ≤20 words OR sit empty (editorial register) OR carry a single civic-compliance surface (entry-control, permit, declaration — registered for government-affiliated sites that have a real compliance gatekeeping role). One primary CTA. No carousel, no interstitial, no forced nav.
pitfalls: Auto-rotating hero carousel (defensible ONLY for touring artists on tour-specific pages — see bobmarley 01/05)
Feature-list-as-hero
Forced-steps funnel before the primary action
Decorative ornament that adds no job
evidence: 7/8 vision-seen sites pass this criterion
bobmarley has 5-up carousel (01/05) — defensible only because it's a tour-CITY carousel for a touring artist; not a generic product carousel

visitbarbados: hero is a compliance banner — 'Arriving in Barbados soon? Please fill out your Online Customs and Immigration form' — registered one-job-per-screen = compliance, not aspiration. Whitelist for civic-compliance surfaces.
socanews: H1 = body size (14px = 14px), 4-of-7 imgs are the logo itself — typographic-hierarchy failure mode flagged at C3/C4
criteria.v0_1_change: v0.1's C5 retained; one narrow exemption noted (touring-artist carousel is legitimate) to prevent v0.1's implicit 'no carousel ever' over-fitting.

criteria.name: Anti-platform-extraction, transparent commercial surface
criteria.what_it_checks: No extraction-business-model signals: no countdown timers, no fake scarcity widgets, no dynamic-pricing feel, no hidden-fee reveals, no surveillance-theatre blocks, no platform-shells hiding the design. Where money/sale/signup is mentioned, it's literal, plain, complete on first sight.
criteria.observable: Zero countdowns, zero 'only N left' widgets, zero fake strikethrough discounts, zero 'unusual activity' surveillance blocks, zero dynamic-pricing feel. Prices/labels/sale language are literal and complete where present. The site reads as a destination, not a platform funnel. ALSO: the site is renderable to a non-JS visitor — hero and scroll captures are NOT byte-identical, tokens.json has a meaningful title and h1, no 'Bot or Not?' title, no OneTrust raw JS as body text — i.e., the rendering surface itself is not a dark pattern.

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: Every price/CTA is plain, complete, literal. No urgency widgets. No surveillance blocks. Site is a destination, not a funnel.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: No dark patterns, but one or two trust-reassurance cliches ('best price guaranteed' / 'limited time' ribbon) that undercut the plainness.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: A real-pricing-step-to-see-total or a small urgency cue; the page leans funnel-shaped.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: Countdowns, fake scarcity, dynamic-pricing feel, hidden-fee reveals, surveillance blocks, or platform-shells hiding content. (This is the spotify/ticketmaster/travelocity register.)

criteria.generation_rule: No countdowns. No fake scarcity. No dynamic-pricing cues. No hidden fees. No 'unusual activity' surveillance frames. Prices/CTA labels literal and complete on first sight. If you need trust, be transparent — don't add reassurance copy.
pitfalls: Countdown timer / 'only 2 left' widgets
Fake strikethrough discounts
Bait pricing that hides the real total
Reassurance-copy padding
'Detected unusual behavior' / paused-activity frames (extraction-register trap)
Generic SaaS funnel-shapes used because 'best practice'
Bot-wall / cookie-gate-first rendering as a defense (every signal-capable visitor gets the wall first)
Empty SPA shell with hero==scroll byte-identical PNGs (no scrollable content; design IS anti-pattern)
Tokens.json captures raw OneTrust script as body text (the extraction page's first byte is a JS blob, not editorial)
evidence: 0/8 vision-seen positive sites have countdowns/scarcity/dynamic-pricing cues
ticketmaster hero confirmed: 'Your Browsing Activity Has Been Paused' + IP+session-fingerprint displayed in monospace = dark pattern AS the design
spotify hero confirmed: 'Preview of Spotify — Sign up free' gradient band + empty-art-tile grid = platform-shell register
travelocity (negative): tokens.json title = 'Bot or Not?'; body = 'Show us your human side...'; screenshot is the Cloudflare/PerimeterX challenge — extraction-by-perimeter-defense
ticketmaster (negative): tokens.json body is a raw OneTrust optanon script blob; hero PNG is a near-empty 251KB beige surface; Times New Roman fallback = no platform font loaded
spotify (negative): hero.png and scroll.png are byte-identical (1.88MB each); tokens.json h1 = 'Your Library'; SPA shell rendered with no editorial content
criteria.v0_1_alignment: v0.1's C6 retained unchanged. New evidence: ticketmaster itself shows that the dark-pattern register shows itself in the SURFACING of the design (surveillance-theatre), not just in copy. Updated observable.

criteria.name: Imagery rooted in real Caribbean people and practice
criteria.what_it_checks: Imagery depicts specific real Caribbean culture — community, performance, places, lived-in scenes, diaspora gatherings — not stock beach/palm postcard, not posed-generic lifestyle, not 3D abstract mascot art, not platform-gridded generic album art.
criteria.observable: Photography or illustration depicts identifiable real scenes or people with Caribbean/diaspora context. ZERO obvious stock watermarks, ZERO posed-generic lifestyle, ZERO 3D abstract mascots, ZERO beach-palm-tree postcards as the primary visual, ZERO platform-gridded generic album art.

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: Real, specific Caribbean imagery: mas, performers, actual streets, named community events. Documentary weight.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: Real but genericizable (a beach/ocean shot that could be any island), OR a mix of real culture and one stock filler.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Stock beach/palm-tree postcard OR posed-generic lifestyle actors OR platform art-tile grid as primary visual.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: Watermarked stock, 3D abstract mascots, generic art-tile grids, or imagery with no Caribbean context.

criteria.generation_rule: Use real photography of specific Caribbean/diaspora culture — carnival, live performance, actual ocean/streets, community gatherings. Never stock beach/palm postcard. Never posed-generic lifestyle. Never abstract mascots. Never a generic art-tile grid.
pitfalls: Beach/palm-tree postcard cliche
Watermarked stock
Posed-generic lifestyle
3D abstract mascots/blobs
Generic-art-tile grids copied from platform-default pages
evidence: wiadca: carnival-association seal + festival-poster band = real community regalia, NOT stock
koffee: photographic video hero + painted overlay of a real contemporary artist = specific
machel: cinematic B&W portrait of the artist + film festival laurels = documentary weight
spotify (negative): no Caribbean imagery, generic popular-artist tile grid
criteria.v0_1_alignment: v0.1's C7 retained, plus a new pitfall: 'generic-art-tile grid' (added when spotify was vision-confirmed).

criteria.name: Semantic accessibility: a real h1 reading your headline intent
criteria.what_it_checks: The visible hero statement (or its deliberately-absent editorial equivalent) is also the document's primary <h1>. A brand site whose underlying DOM has h1_count=0 ships empty to screen readers, screenshot scrapers, and SEO crawlers — a quiet failure mode often paired with JS-rendered hero regions.
criteria.observable: DOM has exactly one <h1> per visible page; the visible hero copy and the <h1> agree (or the editorial register intentionally omits both).

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: Hero copy and <h1> agree; one <h1> per page; semantic structure traces design hierarchy.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: An h1 exists and roughly matches hero, but the type scale makes it invisible to crawlers/AT (excessively small).

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: An h1 exists but reads corporate boilerplate ('Welcome to our website') with no relation to hero intent.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: h1_count=0 — visitor arriving via screen reader, SEO, or SSR scraper gets no headline. (beyonce, shaggy, shaggy_bio, nkotb all measured h1_count=0 in tokens.json.)

criteria.generation_rule: Design the visible hero headline AND the document <h1> in the same step. If the editorial register wants no visible copy (premium-quiet image-led landing), the absence must itself be an intentional decision, not an oversight. Verify with `document.querySelectorAll('h1').length === 1` and that the content matches what the visitor sees.
pitfalls: JS-rendered hero whose <h1> is missing from server HTML
Hidden h1 reading 'Skip to Main Content' or generic boilerplate while the visible hero is 'act ii' / album-title / event-name
Image-only hero with no textual headline and no h1 fallback
Multiple competing <h1>s (one per section) breaking the document outline
evidence: koffee: <h1> matches the visible hero (working example)
tokens.json: beyonce, shaggy, shaggy_bio, nkotb all measured h1_count=0 — primary failure mode for global/legacy Caribbean-artist sites
fenty (fentybeauty.com): also h1_count=0 — extends the failure mode into the beauty-brand register
criteria.negative_passes_if_offclass: spotify/ticketmaster/travelocity likely h1_count=0 too — measured as Off-class by this criterion (the failure mode).

criteria.name: Reciprocal vs. extractive commercial posture
criteria.what_it_checks: The site's commercial surface is reciprocal (donate / volunteer / become-a-member / sign-in-as-contributor; transparent results and project phases) — NOT extractive (sign-up-to-use / dynamic pricing / hidden fees / opaque royalty splits). For sites with no commercial surface at all (community media, civic body), this is satisfied by default — the absence is the design choice.
criteria.observable: Hero OR scroll exposes at least one RECIPROCAL CTA (Donate / Volunteer / Become a Member / Submit / Publish-with-us / Sign-In-as-contributor), AND the absence of extractive widgets (countdown timers, fake scarcity, 'only N left', dynamic pricing UI, hidden fee reveals, bot-wall/cookie-gate-first rendering). For Caribbean community/industry/festival sites, reciprocal-CTAs are the load-bearing commercial surface; their absence is itself an anti-pattern. For platforms that extract value (spotify/ticketmaster/travelocity), the entire posture is the anti-pattern.

levels.label: On-class
levels.descriptor: At least one reciprocal CTA visible; no extractive widgets; pricing/value extraction either transparent or absent by design.

levels.label: Near
levels.descriptor: Reciprocal CTAs present in scroll but hidden in hero; one or two mild platform-CUA patterns coexist.

levels.label: Partial
levels.descriptor: Sign-up-to-use / premium-only surfaces dominate; donate / become-a-member / sign-in-as-contributor is missing or buried.

levels.label: Off-class
levels.descriptor: The site IS the extraction — bot-wall rendering, dynamic pricing, hidden fees, opaque royalty splits, no bylines. (Spotify/Ticketmaster/Travelocity register.)

criteria.generation_rule: Choose between two postures: (A) RECIPROCAL — the site asks the visitor to participate as a contributor (donate / volunteer / become-a-member / submit / sign-in-as-contributor). Make the reciprocal CTA visible above the fold or in the upper-third of the scroll. (B) NO COMMERCIAL SURFACE — community media / civic body that does not extract from its community. In either case, do not introduce extractive widgets (countdowns, scarcity, dynamic pricing, fees-as-design).
pitfalls: Sign-up-to-use / premium-only CTAs on a community site that should be reciprocal (donate / become-a-member)
Bot-wall / cookie-gate-first rendering as a defense — every signal-capable visitor gets the wall first
Bot-or-Not challenge page captured as the 'homepage' (extraction site's surface IS the anti-pattern)
In-house organizational promos conflated with third-party display advertising (both are different categories; only third-party ads are anti-open-rails)
Hidden pricing extraction: dynamic pricing UI, opaque service fees, royalty splits with no public disclosure
evidence: wiadca: Donate Today (red CTA) + Become a Member + Shop — reciprocal CTAs dominant; secondary ad blocks are in-house (band launches Germany 2026, Atlantic City promo) NOT third-party display ads

ncctt: 'Click Here for Blood Drive' as a community-reciprocal participation surface; publishes Brass Bacchanal 2026 ranked results (Temperate the Band 433, Korm Sumerville & the Sensational Band 405) — reciprocity through transparency
beenieman_dancehallmag: Sign In as a subscription/contributor signal; zero ad slots on hero+scroll; staff named (Claude Mills, DancehallMag Team)
